output.title: Helix HX-5000 Configuration and Troubleshooting Guide

sections.heading: Optics and transceiver health checks
key_facts: On 7.2, reduce DOM polling on affected SFP28 ports by setting the transceiver monitoring interval to 120 seconds.
Keep optics below 50 C case temperature when possible, especially on ports showing bias current spikes or remote LOS alarms.
If a port continues to flap under load, move the optic to a later-release port or replace the module with one that has a stable bias current profile.

sections.heading: Stack stability and master election
key_facts: On 7.3, use matched-length stack cables between all members to reduce master election oscillation.
Keep control-plane load below 60 percent until the software is upgraded, because higher load increases the chance of unstable master changes.
Pin the desired master by setting a higher priority value on the preferred member and avoid adding or removing members during the unstable period.
On 7.6, keep stack cabling under 1 m when possible and avoid chaining all members through a single long physical path.

sections.heading: Spanning tree behavior on access ports
key_facts: Do not run rapid-pvst on ports facing devices that legitimately move multiple MAC addresses, such as virtualization hosts or clustered appliances.
Use a dedicated edge VLAN design or restrict the port to a single access device when rapid-pvst is required.
Apply portfast on edge ports to reduce convergence delay, but only on interfaces that do not participate in downstream bridging.
Monitor for continuous topology-change notifications on 10G access ports and reclassify the port role if the notifications persist.

sections.heading: LACP and EtherChannel member handling
key_facts: On 7.4, configure both ends of the bundle for fast LACP timers if the design permits it.
If the peer advertises slow timers and the bundle mis-bundles or suspends members, switch the local port-channel to fast LACP timers.
When the bundle must remain on slow timers, do not flap individual member links during maintenance and clear the EtherChannel only after link restoration.

sections.heading: EVPN route handling and memory protection
key_facts: On 7.6, trigger a controlled EVPN route refresh after moving the anycast gateway MAC.
Avoid gateway MAC mobility during periods when the fabric is carrying active type-5 routes, and keep the gateway anchored on a single leaf pair when possible.
On 7.6, reduce unnecessary neighbor resets and schedule a reload before free memory drops below 15 percent.
If route-refresh events are unavoidable, keep EVPN adjacency changes out of peak traffic windows.

sections.heading: Queue, buffer, and burst management
key_facts: On 7.2, reduce burstiness with upstream shaping or spread load across additional uplinks so no single egress port stays above 85 percent sustained utilization.
For critical low-latency flows on oversubscribed 100G egress ports, reserve a dedicated queue on the affected interface.
On 8.0, limit multicast fanout on busy leafs or move replication-heavy workloads onto a separate uplink group to protect the shared buffer pool.
If multicast bursts are predictable, schedule the traffic outside congestion-sensitive windows and tune the multicast reservation to 12 percent with a 4096 cell queue limit where required.
